definition: Generative Pre-trained Transformer 4 (GPT-4) is a large language model developed by OpenAI and the fourth in its series of GPT foundation models.
details: GPT-4 is preceded by GPT-3.5 and followed by its successor GPT-5. GPT-4V is a version of GPT-4 that can process images in addition to text. OpenAI has not revealed technical details and statistics about GPT-4, such as the precise size of the model. An early version of GPT-4 was integrated by Microsoft into Bing Chat, launched in February 2023. GPT-4 was released in ChatGPT in March 2023, and removed in 2025. GPT-4 is still available in OpenAI's API.

explainer.lead: GPT-4 is OpenAI’s fourth general-purpose GPT model, able to work with text and images and to connect with outside tools such as web search. Released in March 2023, it powered widely used assistants and showed strong coding and test performance, while its hallucinations, biases, and undisclosed design remained important concerns.

tiers.eli5: GPT-4 is like a very well-read assistant that guesses what should come next in a conversation, then gets coached by people to give safer, more useful answers. It can look at a picture as well as read words, so you might show it a photo and ask a question about it. It can sound confident while being wrong, so its answers still need checking.
tiers.practitioner: GPT-4 has been used through products and APIs for coding assistance, image-grounded question answering, and web-enabled workflows that insert tool results into the prompt. The default release offered an 8K-token context window and a special API version supported 32K tokens; GPT-4 Turbo later raised this to 128K. Validate outputs carefully because GPT-4 can hallucinate, generate vulnerable code, and provide post-hoc explanations that contradict its earlier statements.
tiers.paperLevel: GPT-4 is OpenAI’s fourth GPT foundation model, released on March 14, 2023; its parameter count, architecture, hardware, dataset construction, and optimization settings were not disclosed. Training combined supervised next-token prediction, informally p(x_t | x_<t), with reinforcement learning using human and AI feedback, and the model accepts text and image inputs. Known limits include hallucination, unverifiable post-hoc rationales, possible cognitive biases, and scores below 33% in every category of the visual ConceptARC abstract-reasoning benchmark.

usedIn.name: ChatGPT Plus
usedIn.detail: Provided GPT-4 to subscribers in 2023 and later added plugins, browsing, image uploads, voice interaction, and DALL-E 3 integration.

usedIn.name: Microsoft Copilot
usedIn.detail: Launched as Bing Chat on February 7, 2023, using the Microsoft Prometheus model built on top of GPT-4.

usedIn.name: Healthcare administration
usedIn.detail: Microsoft and Epic Systems announced GPT-4-powered systems to help providers answer patient questions and analyse medical records.

usedIn.name: Software development
usedIn.detail: Programmers used GPT-4 to find code errors, suggest optimizations, and accelerate tasks such as porting a program from MATLAB to Python.

components.name: Text and image input
components.detail: Accepts written prompts and, unlike its predecessors, images as input.

components.name: Context window
components.detail: Held 8K tokens by default, with a special API version supporting up to 32K tokens.

components.name: Next-token prediction core
components.detail: Was initially trained on large datasets of internet text to predict the next token, roughly corresponding to a word.

components.name: Feedback-based tuning
components.detail: Used reinforcement learning with human and AI feedback, including training to refuse prompts classified as harmful by OpenAI.

components.name: External-interface prompting
components.detail: Can emit formatted requests for web searches or other tools, then use the returned information to form a response.

flow: Text and optionally an image enter the model within its context window.
GPT-4 processes the prompt and predicts a response token by token.
If instructed, it emits a formatted request such as <search>query</search>.
Tool results are added to the prompt, and GPT-4 forms its response.
explainer.origin: OpenAI finished training GPT-4 on August 8, 2022 and released it on March 14, 2023, after internal adversarial testing by dedicated red teams. Its technical report withheld model size, architecture, hardware, and detailed training settings, citing competition and safety; Sam Altman said training cost more than $100 million.
explainer.lineage: GPT-4 followed GPT-3.5, which underpinned ChatGPT, and was later followed by GPT-5. GPT-4V handles images and text, while the November 2023 GPT-4 Turbo line added a 128K context window and lower pricing. OpenAI introduced GPT-4o on May 13, 2024 for real-time text, audio, and image processing and generation, and replaced GPT-4 with GPT-4o in ChatGPT in April 2025.
explainer.whyItMatters: GPT-4 brought multimodal input, tool use, and stronger coding and exam performance into mainstream assistants, including a USMLE result more than 20 points above passing in Microsoft research. Its medical and security errors, weak ConceptARC results, and opaque explanations show why high test scores do not establish reliable reasoning or safe deployment.

diagram.caption: GPT-4 can respond directly or loop through an external tool, whose output is added to its prompt.
